The provided data outlines the characteristics of newly diagnosed children and adolescents at their first contact in the care pathway, serving as the basis for [[indikator-1b|Indikator 1b]] [^src1]. In total, the cohort comprises 210 newly diagnosed patients [^src1]. Because this analysis is based on a single reporting period from the 2025 dataset, no longitudinal trends can be established from this data alone [^src1].

Regarding diagnoses, [[crohns-sygdom|Crohns sygdom]] is the leading condition, accounting for 134 patients (64%), while [[colitis-ulcerosa|Colitis ulcerosa]] follows as the secondary diagnosis with 76 patients (36%) [^src1]. No patients were recorded with primary sclerosing cholangitis or short bowel syndrome in this specific dataset, making them clear trailers with zero reported cases [^src1].

Demographically, males represent the majority of the cohort with 116 patients (55%) compared to 94 females (45%) [^src1]. The average age at diagnosis is 13 years (range 0-17), with a median age of 14 years (Q1-Q3: 12-16) [^src1]. When evaluating age groups, the vast majority of patients are adolescents aged 10-17 years, making up 188 patients (90%) and acting as the clear leader in age distribution [^src1]. Younger age groups are significantly less represented, acting as trailers: 17 patients (8%) are aged 6-9, 4 patients (2%) are aged 2-5, and fewer than five (marked as # to preserve anonymity) fall into the 0-1 year category, which stands out as a statistical outlier due to its extreme rarity [^src1].

In terms of healthcare utilization, these patients had an average of 17 contacts (range 1-50) and a median of 16 contacts (Q1-Q3: 10-22) [^src1]. Physical contacts are the dominant mode of interaction, totaling 1,355 contacts (61%), compared to 872 virtual contacts (39%) [^src1].
